questions.prompt: A new Blob container must require encryption scope tenant-a for every upload. Which configuration enforces that?

options.text: Set tenant-a as default and prevent encryption-scope overrides.
options.explanation: Uploads cannot choose a different encryption boundary.

options.text: Set tenant-a as default but permit overrides.
Add a container metadata entry named tenant-a.
options.explanation: Metadata does not enforce encryption selection.

options.text: Assign Storage Blob Data Reader to tenant-a.
options.explanation: A role assignment does not set the container encryption scope.

questions.prompt: A previously readable blob starts returning 403 immediately after its encryption scope is disabled. Permissions and network paths are unchanged. What should be checked?

options.text: Re-enable the required scope after confirming the change was unintended.
options.explanation: Disabled scopes prevent operations that depend on them.
Authorization key rotation does not re-enable an encryption scope.
Anonymous authorization cannot restore a disabled encryption dependency.
Version IDs are not an encryption-scope availability control.

questions.prompt: A team configures different Blob encryption scopes for two customers. What still needs separate configuration?

options.text: Authorization deciding which customer may read each blob.
options.explanation: Encryption-key boundaries do not replace access-control assignments.

options.text: No authorization is needed because scope names authenticate users.
options.explanation: A scope name is not an identity credential.

options.text: Every scope automatically issues a customer SAS.
options.explanation: Scope creation does not distribute access tokens.

options.text: Each scope automatically creates its own storage firewall.
options.explanation: Network rules belong to a separate account/network configuration.
